notes: `עֶרְוַת דָּבָר` is split attributively as the ASV renders it (rule 28); reading the pair as one indivisible idiom was the competing analysis.
`בְּקֶרֶב` is split because the ASV writes a word for each morpheme; `לִפְנֵי` fuses to *before* under rule 30 and `מֵאַחֲרֵי` to *from* headed on the governing first morpheme under rule 23.
The waw of `וְלֹא־יִרְאֶה` takes the purpose *that* written for it (rule 55).
